summary:
Status: complete.

Summary: Added sccache compilation caching and sharded nextest e2e runs using only workflow/config/doc files in `/Users/sachinkoli/.hoocode/worktrees/noteapp/ci-cache` (branch `agent/ci-cache`, uncommitted as required). No src, Cargo, or toolchain changes; no job restructuring.

Files changed:
- `.config/nextest.toml` (new): `ci` profile (`slow-timeout 120s`, no fail-fast) plus an override giving the single serial `end_to_end` test a 1500s slow-timeout and 0 retries; header comments explain the sharding model and that plain `cargo test` is untouched.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: 2-shard matrix (`shard: ["1/2","2/2"]`, so 2 OS × 2 shards), sccache via `mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.11` with `SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED=true`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=2G`; `rust-cache` gains `shared-key: ${{ matrix.os }}` so shards share one target-dir cache; nextest via `taiki-e/install-action@v2` (`nextest@0.9.151`); test step is now `cargo nextest run --locked --profile ci --partition count:${{ matrix.shard }}`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (macos + linux jobs) and `release-binaries.yml` (macos universal + linux jobs): same sccache env + setup step, kept alongside existing rust-cache; no nextest (build-only packaging).
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: short "CI caching and sharding" paragraph with local opt-ins (`RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo build`, `cargo nextest run`).

Verification output:
- `ruby -ryaml`: ci.yml, release.yml, release-binaries.yml all parse OK. `python tomllib`: nextest.toml parses OK.
- Real `cargo-nextest 0.9.151` binary (prebuilt universal-apple-darwin tarball, verified release tag): `run --help` confirms `--locked` and `--partition count:M/N` support; a scratch crate with a copy of the config ran `nextest list --profile ci --partition count:1/2` and `count:2/2` with exit 0 and no config errors (validates profile/override/filter schema).
- `git status`: only the 4 files above modified plus untracked `.config/`; zero src changes. Stray `target/` from the probe build removed. Not run: full workspace `nextest list`/CI itself — this Mac lacks the Metal toolchain so even plain `cargo test --no-run` fails here (pre-existing local limitation, unrelated to this change); sccache/nextest pins were verified against live GitHub release metadata.

Expected wall-clock win + reasoning: moderate, honest accounting. (1) sccache's big win is warm-cache compiles across pushes/PRs, most on mac jobs where release-binaries does two full universal target builds — second and later runs skip recompiling unchanged crates. (2) Sharding does *not* shorten the e2e suite itself: all 22 chapters run inside one serial `#[gpui::test]`, so it lands whole on one shard and stays the long pole. The win is isolating it on its own runner (no CPU contention with the ~30 shell unit-test modules, which get a full runner to themselves) plus shared warm caches. 2 shards is the sweet spot; more would idle behind the e2e shard. True per-chapter sharding needs splitting that one test — a src change, explicitly out of lane.

Open questions:
- CI still installs floating `stable` while the repo pins 1.98 in rust-toolchain.toml; cache keys stay correct regardless (both caches key on actual rustc), but pinning CI to the file would make warm hits more stable — left alone as out of lane (toolchain/job structure).
- `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=2G` is a judgment call to protect the 10 GB repo cache next to rust-cache; tune after observing hit rates (`sccache --show-stats` isn't printed — could add if wanted).
- Sibling crew's release+dev double-build removal will compose cleanly (this change only adds steps/env, no step reordering of build commands).
